articles.title: Tired of heat and storms? Visit these places to enjoy fall’s beauty
articles.summary: The weather could be warmer in some places or wetter in others, thanks to El Niño. Here are five places to find classic fall conditions and plenty to do.
articles.body: There’s no time like October when it comes to leaf-peeping. Each day beyond the autumn equinox ushers in darker days and cooler temperatures — the cues for leaves to change color. Across the country, trees and shrubs shut down the production of their energy-making chlorophyll, the pigment behind their lush greens, leaving behind vivid forests of yellows, oranges and reds. This year, lingering warmth could disrupt or shorten the fall foliage window for large portions of the country. During El Niño years, the Pacific jet stream shifts south, which means hiking conditions in the Northeast could be warmer and drier than usual, while treks in parts of the southern US could be wetter. So, CNN’s Weather and Travel teams partnered to identify North American destinations most likely to experience a picture-perfect autumn this year, based on their weather and climate history. These are five places we think you’ll still find the best mix of classic fall conditions and plenty to do. Upper Green Mountains, Vermont The tradition of leaf-peeping in Vermont goes back decades, but the Upper Green Mountains area, a perennial favorite for fall foliage, and other regions of the state continue to offer visitors new ways to take in the changing colors, including ziplining and visits to cideries. For tourists who love to hike, it would be difficult to exhaust all the options — the state is known for the Green Mountains, after all, and the 272-mile Long Trail. Cyclists who visit the Upper Green Mountains in the fall also have lots of options, including trails at the nearby von Trapp Family Lodge and Resort in Stowe, which is owned by descendants of the Austrian family made famous in the 1965 Hollywood musical, “The Sound of Music.” Visitors can also combine two New England institutions by taking a covered bridge tour to view fall foliage; in Montgomery, there are five remaining bridges, the most of any town in Vermont. Beyond enjoying Vermont’s unique outdoorsy culture, visitors can take home local goodies such as maple syrup. One place that many tourists visit on their way to the Upper Green Mountains is Dakin Farm, whose large farm store in Ferrisburgh in the Champlain Valley is bursting with samples, especially of Vermont cheese. “We’re extremely busy,” Sam Cutting, the company’s CEO, told CNN Travel, adding that the last two weekends of September were busier than last year. “Now is a great time to come.” Vermont is one of the prime destinations for fall foliage in the Northeast. While the state is home to just 640,000 people, a whopping 4 million visitors travel to Vermont each fall, accounting for $1 billion in economic impact, according to state officials. Consult the foliage tracker that Vermont keeps in September and October for tips on where to see the most vivid displays of fall color. The weather to expect: High temperatures drop from the 50s to the 40s Fahrenheit (15 to 4 degrees Celsius) in October at higher elevations, while the valleys stay a bit milder. This year, temperatures aren’t expected to stray far from that norm through at least mid-October, possibly longer. Peak color has already arrived in the mountains, and colors are starting to change in lower elevations too, ahead of their mid-October peak, according to ExploreFall.com, a website that tracks fall foliage across the United States. Blue Ridge Mountains, North Carolina In the Southeast, Asheville stands out all year round but it’s especially spectacular in the fall. One of the best places to enjoy the foliage in the Asheville area is the Blue Ridge Parkway, a 469-mile marvel through Appalachia that can often seem like one long scenic drive. In 2025, 16.5 million people visited the park, which courses through North Carolina and Virginia, including 2 million visitors in the month of October alone, according to the National Park Service. The region has weathered, quite literally, some difficult times in the past few years, after Hurricane Helene blew through in 2024 and devastated parts of the Asheville area, including Historic Biltmore Village. But since going full force on recovery, the region has seen a return of tourists. And the mountain scenery that has long drawn visitors remains as enchanting as ever. The sections of the Blue Ridge Parkway closest to Asheville are completely open, according to the Blue Ridge Parkway external affairs office. There are still intermittent closures and construction connected to recovery projects, and the park service recommends consulting the road status section of its website when traveling to the region. Since there are significant elevation variations in the Asheville area, parts of the region will see peak fall color at different times, tourism officials say. Among the highlights are Pisgah National Forest for traditional leaf-peeping activities, and artistic craft centers such as the Folk Art Center for shopping. Beyond the parkway and downtown Asheville, which is a cultural hotspot with one-of-a-kind mountain charm, other popular stops in the area include Biltmore Estate, the 250-room Vanderbilt mansion, which was largely spared hurricane damage. The property offers a rooftop tour, which provides a unique vantage point on the leaves. But a visit there isn’t just a house tour; it’s an opportunity to hike and bike the historic, 8,000-acre property. There are walking trails along the French Broad River and 20 miles of biking trails as well. Visitors can take horse-drawn carriage rides. The weather to expect: High temperatures fall from the lower 70s in early October to the 50s by mid-November (22 to 10 C) but expect it to be cooler in the mountains. Fall is usually a drier period, but this year, odds are leaning toward above-average rainfall. “The Asheville area has experienced periods of dry and rainy weather this summer but is largely drought-free compared to surrounding regions,” said Bill Quade, Biltmore’s director of horticulture. “This supports a healthier and more vibrant leaf display.” Low to moderate color is already dotting trees in the area, according to ExploreFall.com. Peak color is usually mid-to-late October in the mountains and early November in valleys. Nova Scotia, Canada Foliage tourists in Nova Scotia can soak up autumn’s glory across the Canadian province. Many visitors make a beeline for Cape Breton in the eastern corner of the province, a wild island offering a variety of outdoor activities for viewing the changing leaves. Cape Breton Highlands National Park is especially popular with visitors who enjoy the Skyline Trail on the western section of the property, which overlooks the Gulf of St. Lawrence where whales are often seen. (Moose are also spotted in the park – but a lot closer). There’s also a series of breathtaking waterfalls in the park. Toward the province’s other end, visitors can take a boat tour or kayak along the coast of the Bay of Fundy, located between New Brunswick and Nova Scotia. They can also enjoy the changing leaves while on whale watching excursions. The Annapolis Valley, northwest of the city of Halifax, is home to picturesque vineyards that offer tastings. The region’s wineries provide a sample of what Nova Scotia produces — not just wine, but also local food including can’t-miss lobster, oysters and scallops. At Benjamin Bridge winery, for example, visitors can enjoy a glass of Riesling and a meal on an open-air patio while enjoying foliage views. Other wineries include Bent Ridge Winery, which is also home to Bent Nail Brewery. Beyond traditional leaf-peeping hikes, visitors can also play golf, which draws visitors to Nova Scotia year-round. Among the top-rated courses available are Cape Breton Highlands Links in Ingonish, and Bell Bay Golf Club, which overlooks Baddeck Bay. Visitors can also stay overnight at golf resorts in stunning locations, including Digby Pines in Digby and The Lakes Golf Club & Resort in Ben Eoin. The weather to expect: Highs in the 50s are typical in October (15 C), and this year isn’t expected to stray too far from that, according to Environment Canada, the country’s weather and climate agency. Fall color is best through mid-October in the Cape Breton area. North Central New Mexico Fall foliage visits to the Santa Fe area offer typical leaf-peeping activities not unlike what you find in East Coast destinations but with a flair particular to the Southwest. That’s because, for starters, the tree canopy in Sante Fe is dominated by aspens, which turn a golden yellow hue in the fall, rather than the sugar maples and beech trees you find in New England and along the East Coast. Exploring the Santa Fe National Forest Scenic Byway will provide visitors with opportunities for biking, camping and picnicking amid the changing leaves. At Hyde Memorial State Park, visitors can even opt to camp in yurts. And for a one-of-a-kind experience, the Ski Santa Fe resort offers chairlift rides in the fall that allow visitors to glimpse the aspens from up high. The festive atmosphere includes a beer garden and live music. New Mexico offers a longer window to enjoy fall foliage and one signature event that provides a unique complement to the season takes place in Taos, about an hour north of Sante Fe. It’s called the Taos Mountain Balloon Rally, and it’s scheduled for October 24 and 25. In addition to ballooning, the event includes a parade and a grand ball. The Enchanted Circle Scenic Byway, which links the towns of Taos, Red River and Angel Fire, begins in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, where the state’s signature aspens are mixed with evergreens. The weather to expect: Highs fall from the 60s to the 50s in October and November in Santa Fe (20 to 10 C). Prepare for cooler highs in the mountains, which generally range in the 40s and 50s in October (4 to 15 C). It’s been a wetter than usual start to fall thanks indirectly to El Niño, which has upped the number of Pacific storms that eventually funneled moisture into the region. But there are equal chances that the trend flips in the next month of the season. The mountains are already seeing high to peak color, according to ExploreFall.com, which is right on time. Vancouver Island, British Columbia West Coast leaf-peepers flock to Vancouver Island in Canada’s British Columbia province. The region has a mild climate, and its beaches and lakes offer a host of opportunities for water activities during the fall, including whale watching, kayaking and paddleboarding. One place close to the city of Victoria, which is at the island’s southern tip, is The Butchart Gardens, a National Historic Site of Canada and a place whose blooms inspire photographers. The Japanese Garden, featuring maple trees and a pair of copper beeches that frame the Torii Gate, is especially beautiful in autumn. Not far away, Goldstream Provincial Park in Langford is home to what tourism officials call Niagara Falls of the West Coast, in addition to big-leaf maples, red alders that turn golden, along with 600-year-old Douglas fir trees. In the fall, there’s an annual salmon run there, and it’s also a good spot for viewing eagles. For visitors ready for a road trip, there are small coastal towns to explore on Vancouver Island, including Campbell River. About three hours north of Victoria, it’s known as the Salmon Fishing Capital of the World. Nearby, the Elk Falls Suspension Bridge provides a stunning viewing platform of a gushing waterfall below. Port Hardy, on the northern tip of the island about a five-and-a-half-hour drive from Victoria, is home to Great Bear Lodge, where in addition to viewing fall foliage, visitors can take a tour to spot grizzly bears. The weather to expect: Highs in the 50s are the norm in October in Victoria (10 to 15 C). This year could be a bit warmer at times since warmer-than-average temperatures are expected in October, according to Environment Canada. It’s also the start of the wet season, so that means there’s a greater chance of rain and cloud cover. The best autumn colors appear in October, according to The Butchart Gardens’ website, but exactly when in the month is weather-dependent. Seasonably mild days and mix of sun and clouds plus cool nights are expected through mid-October. Those ideal fall conditions could help foliage really pop, especially the reds.

articles.title: Greens investigate party member behind Zionism motion
articles.summary: It has emerged Lubna Speitan was listed in court documents as a "close friend" of a man later jailed for supporting al-Qaeda.
articles.body:
The Green Party has launched an investigation into party member Lubna Speitan, after it emerged she was listed in court documents as a "close friend" of a man later jailed for supporting al-Qaeda.

Speitan was behind a controversial Green Party conference motion which described Zionism as a form of racism.

A Green Party spokesperson said: "Where members have expressed views that do not fit in with the party's values, we have internal processes to investigate and an investigation is underway."

In a post on Instagram, before the Green Party had confirmed its investigation to the BBC, Speitan said: "I reject all defamatory and nonsense claims made about me."

She added: "I reject all attempts to decontextualise past statements I have made."

"This is a classic distraction. I am not the conversation," she said, adding: "Racism is. Zionism is. The ethnic cleansing and genocide of Palestinians is. Let's talk about that."

In June, a UN commission of inquiry said Israel had deliberately targeted Palestinian children, resulting in genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes in the Gaza Strip.

Israel has repeatedly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide and says they are justified as a means of self-defence.

Polanski banned from Israel after party's motion declaring 'Zionism is racism'

Green member behind Zionism motion named as 'close friend' of jailed al-Qaeda supporter in court

Speitan, a British-Palestinian artist, proposed the Green Party conference motion defining Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state".

The motion - which was approved by party members by 1,022 votes to 813 - also called for a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine".

Under Green Party rules, motions supported by members become official party policy, but will not necessarily be included in the party's manifesto at the next general election.

The motion attracted criticism from opposition parties and some Jewish groups, who labelled it an "attack on the Jewish community".

Four out of five Green Party MPs also opposed the motion.

Adrian Ramsay, a former party leader and Green MP for Waveney Valley, said the motion was an "unhelpful distraction" and "wrong in principle" as "the Green Party has always supported the right to self-determination and that has to apply to all peoples".

Asked if he would consider leaving the party, Ramsay told Matt Chorley on BBC Radio 5 Live he was "not ruling anything in or out at this stage".

"What I'm doing at this stage, and we're only a few days after the motion, is to talk carefully with colleagues to reflect both with Jewish Greens but also with Green MPs and other people in leading roles in the party to look at how best can we get things back on track," he said.

On Tuesday, the Jewish Chronicle reported the existence of a 2015 letter from Speitan in which she offered to testify as a defence witness in the trial of Minh Quang Pham.

US prosecutors said Pham had been directed by al-Qaeda leader Anwar al-Awlaki to detonate explosives in Heathrow's arrivals area after spending several months in Yemen being trained by him.

He was jailed for 40 years in the US after pleading guilty to supporting al-Qaeda. He denied planning a suicide attack.

In US court documents from 2015, Speitan was listed as a "close friend" who could provide "critical testimony regarding Pham's mental state".

In a later letter to the US District Judge, Speitan said Pham was one of the "few people I regard with such high respect and esteem".

She said if the judge "truly knew the Minh [Pham] that I and others grew to love and respect", they may have "probably had the whole case dismissed".

She acknowledged he "may have had and developed some behavioural issues" but added: "He turned out to be one of the kindest, honest, most sincere, trustworthy and respectful people I have ever known."

There is no suggestion in the documents Speitan knew of Pham's criminal activities at the time they knew each other.

Following the emergence of the letter on Tuesday afternoon, a Green Party spokesperson said: "Where members have expressed views that do not fit in with the party's values, we have internal processes to investigate."

On Wednesday, the party released an updated statement adding "an investigation is under way".

The spokesperson said: "Lubna Speitan holds no party positions other than being a member."

articles.title: Bubba Watson a sus 47 años: "Me encantaría ser el campeón de mayor edad del Masters de Augusta”
articles.standfirst: El estadounidense visita por primera vez Madrid y disputa desde este jueves el Open de España
articles.summary: El estadounidense visita por primera vez Madrid y disputa desde este jueves el Open de España
articles.body: Este año el Open de España cuenta con la presencia de Bubba Watson (Bagdad, Florida, 47 años), todo un bicampeón del Masters de Augusta (2012 y 2014). Bubba es la sorpresa de un gran plantel de jugadores internacionales y su presencia ayuda a dar lustre al torneo. Fue el jugador de moda hace poco más de una década y alcanzó el número 2 del ranking mundial. Después se enroló en LIV y ahora es el 415, pero inició una interesante remontada en Valderrama, donde acabó noveno en el torneo LIV Golf Andalucía. Ha aterrizado en Madrid por primera vez y está disfrutando mucho de la ciudad en compañía de su mujer. “Este año cuando estuvimos en Valderrama vimos la ciudad y la playa. Mis hijos estuvieron allí; les encanta estar cerca del agua. Luego fuimos al Peñón de Gibraltar; hicimos turismo por la zona y subimos hasta allí. Y ahora, mi esposa ha estado conmigo estos últimos días, así que hemos recorrido la ciudad de Madrid. Intentamos hacer turismo, conocer la cultura y aprender cosas nuevas. Ha sido muy agradable venir a España y ver lugares tan hermosos”, detalla Watson a MARCA. Al golfista le gustaría acudir al Bernabéu el sábado a presenciar el partido entre el Real Madrid y el Villarreal (21.00 h.), y en este sentido lanza un SOS: “Estoy intentando conseguir entradas para ir a verlo. Nunca he ido a un partido de... bueno, nosotros lo llamamos ‘soccer’. Nunca he ido a un partido de fútbol así que sería divertido verlo”. El futuro del icónico jugador estadounidense no está en LIV Golf ahora mismo y ha comenzado a buscarse la vida por ‘fuera’. “¿Por qué he venido a este torneo? Bueno, en primer lugar, porque me dieron una invitación, pero tengo que decir que jugar aquí es un honor y un privilegio. Ya sabes, con el cierre de LIV, necesito un sitio donde jugar y el DP World Tour me ha permitido participar en un par de torneos. Siempre he querido jugar aquí. El campo está algo blando este año, pero es precioso. Madrid es una ciudad hermosa, así que es un sueño venir aquí y conocer este lugar tan bonito”, confiesa. Los resultados del mítico golfistas han mejorado en las últimas semanas y él se siente más competitivo, como él confirma: “Creo que se trata simplemente de jugar con más inteligencia, mantener la concentración y embocar algunos putts más. Pero mi swing está justo donde quiero que esté ahora mismo. Estoy pegando mucho mejor los golpes de salida, lo que me deja en buena posición para ejecutar mejores golpes hacia el green. Ahora todo se reduce a embocar los putts, algo que he estado haciendo bastante bien en los últimos meses”. Hace unos años Watson habló abiertamente de los importantes problemas que padecía. Sufría Trastorno por Déficit de Atención e Hiperactividad (TDAH) y problemas de ansiedad, pero hasta entonces nadie lo sabía y a veces incluso se hacían bromas a su costa. Esto afectó a su salud mental y física, y a nivel deportivo se dejaba notar. En su caso, además sufría de ansiedad social y no se sentía cómodo rodeado de mucha gente. Los comentarios negativos le afectaban mucho y llegó al punto de no poder dormir o hacerlo poco. Perdió peso –se quedó en 73 kg y mide 1,90- e incluso temió por su vida. A veces pensaba en su padre, un exboina verde que padecía trastorno de estrés postraumático y que falleció de cáncer en 2010. En varias ocasiones, Watson creyó estar sufriendo un infarto y tuvo que ser hospitalizado. Watson salió de todo esto y no explica cómo. “Yo lo que tuve que hacer fue hablar con la gente: hablar con mi esposa y con mis amigos cercanos, y compartir con ellos lo que me pasaba. Por eso, lo primero que le diría a cualquiera es que busque a alguien de confianza con quien hablar y le cuente sus problemas. En realidad, no se trata tanto de que te den consejos. El simple hecho de expresar tus problemas en voz alta te ayuda a afrontarlos mejor: en lugar de guardártelo todo, lo compartes y lo dejas salir. En mi caso, hablar con mi esposa y admitir qué fallaba o que era débil en ciertos aspectos, me liberó mentalmente y me ayudó a superar algunos de los problemas que estaba atravesando”, especifica. El ganador de 12 torneos del PGA Tour se queda pensando cuando le preguntamos qué es lo mejor que le ha dado el golf y se ve limitado a acotar su respuesta a los últimos años: “En esta etapa de mi vida, mi esposa y yo jugamos mucho al golf juntos; así pasamos tiempo el uno con el otro. El golf nos ha unido más y nos ha llevado a muchos lugares del mundo donde hemos podido compartir tiempo juntos. Creo que nuestra relación se fortalece cuando podemos pasar tiempo juntos, y el golf ha contribuido a esa unión porque a ella le encanta este deporte”. Bubba se siente bien y promete guerra, sobre todo en Major que le ha otorgado la gloria. “¿Una tercera chaqueta verde? Eso espero. Me estoy esforzando mucho. Ya sabes, he jugado bien allí. Me encantaría ser uno de los campeones de mayor edad, o el de mayor edad, en Augusta. Sería un escenario soñado intentar ponerme esa tercera chaqueta”. Recordemos que el ganador de mayor edad es Jack Nicklaus, con 46 años y 82 días. Bubba ya está en edad de batirlo. Finalmente ponemos en un aprieto al floridano ahora que se ha convertido en todo un jugador internacional, gracias especialmente a LIV Golf. ¿Necesita el golf un quinto grande y que no esté asentado en Estados Unidos? “Es una buena pregunta. No sé si realmente hace falta, pero estaría bien tenerlo. La cuestión es: ¿Dónde se celebraría? Mucha gente votaría para que fuera en su propia sede. Pero sí, sería interesante tener otro Major fuera de Estados Unidos en el que todos aspiraran a competir. La pregunta es dónde sería. Me imagino perfectamente un quinto torneo Major en algún lugar, especialmente fuera de Estados Unidos, ya que hoy en día es un deporte global. Hace 50 años no lo era, pero ahora sí. Así que sí, sería algo estupendo”.

articles.title: LIV Golf: Jon Rahm to leave league over 'unacceptable' terms for LIV 2.0
articles.summary: Jon Rahm will leave LIV Golf after deeming the terms for LIV 2.0 "unacceptable", his lawyer has told a bankruptcy court hearing.
articles.body:
Jon Rahm will leave LIV Golf after deeming the proposed terms for LIV 2.0 "unacceptable", his lawyer has told a bankruptcy court hearing.

The league, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September after Saudi Arabia withdrew its multibillion-dollar funding, has secured a possible $300m in financing from BC Partners Credit in order to try to move forward with the 2027 season.

Rahm's lawyer, John Beck, told the hearing the 31-year-old Spaniard "independently reviewed the terms of LIV 2.0 and determined those terms are unacceptable as to him".

It was later said that LIV and Rahm's representatives are "in advanced discussions for a consensual separation agreement between Mr Rahm and LIV".

It is hoped this will be finalised by a court hearing on 5 November.

LIV's participants are owed at least $45m (£33m) and have the option to leave.

However, the agreement secures an extension for the league to discuss terms with its players, with talks now open until 25 October.

Documents outlining the money owed to LIV Golf's creditors with the 30 largest unsecured claims show that two-time major winner Rahm tops the list with an unsecured claim of $7.5m (£5.5m).

BBC Sport understands there is no obligation on players to sign on to LIV 2.0, regardless of whether they had previously signed multi-year contracts with LIV Golf.

Spain's Rahm was arguably the most high-profile name to join LIV when he left the PGA Tour in December 2023 for a deal worth a reported £222m ($300m).

Some players, including Brooks Koepka, have since returned to the PGA Tour, which rewrote its rules in December to allow the five-time major winner to come back, subject to certain sanctions.

Rahm did not follow suit and remained under long-term contract with LIV, but in May reached a deal with the DP World Tour - formerly the European Tour - to retain his membership and remain eligible for next year's Ryder Cup.

In August, the former world number one won his third straight LIV season title.

He has previously said he had no regrets over joining LIV and backed organisers to make it sustainable.

articles.standfirst: El golfista español no jugará el curso que viene en la versión 2.0 del renovado circuito
articles.summary: El golfista español no jugará el curso que viene en la versión 2.0 del renovado circuito
articles.body: La etapa de Jon Rahm como jugador de LIV Golf ha terminado. El golfista ha decidido abandonar la liga y no jugará en LIV 2.0 en 2027, noticia avanzada por NUCLR Golf que puede confirmar MARCA. Esta mañana los abogados del vasco lo han confirmado durante una audiencia en un tribunal de quiebras de EE.UU. Precisamente LIV anunció ayer que BC Partners Credit aportará una inversión de 300 millones de dólares (unos 265 millones de euros) para el nuevo proyecto LIV 2.0, pero el golfistas vizcaíno ya no formará parte del mismo. Los jugadores tienen hasta el día 25 para decidir si se enrolan en esta nueva aventura o separan sus caminos de los nuevos gestores. La nueva versión constará de 10 torneos, cinco de ellos en Estados Unidos, y los premios bajarán de forma estrepitosa. Los planes del ‘León de Barrika’ de cara al año que viene se desconocen, si bien es miembro del DP World Tour y puede competir en este circuito. Este año el PGA Tour abrió la puerta a Brooks Koepka –previo pago de una donación y quedando fuera de los beneficios que obtienen los jugadores- y esa misma oferta fue extensible para Rahm, DeChambeau y Cam Smith, si bien estos decidieron seguir en LIV. El Fondo de Inversión Pública de Arabia Saudí (PIF) anunció en abril que dejaba de financiar la liga y desde entonces ha existido mucha incertidumbre. Las ganancias de Jon Rahm mientras ha competido en LIV Golf, aparte de su prima de fichaje, ascienden a 96 millones de dólares. Fichó por esta liga en 2023 y su primera temporada fue la 2024; desde entonces ha ganado cuatro torneos (y jugó cuatro desempates) y se proclamó campeón del circuito las tres temporada en las que ha competido allí gracias a su increíble regularidad.

articles.title: Jon Rahm Planning to Leave LIV Post-Bankruptcy, Lawyer Says
articles.summary: Rahm was LIV’s biggest star besides Bryson DeChambeau.
articles.body:
Jon Rahm will not participate in the next iteration of LIV Golf.

"Rahm has independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0, as the parties have been referring to it, and has determined that those terms are unacceptable as to him, and he will not be participating going forward in LIV 2.0," his lawyer, John Beck of Dentons, LLP, said during a hearing in the league's Chapter 11 bankruptcy case in New Jersey on Wednesday.

Rahm has multiple years left on his LIV contract that he signed ahead of the 2024 season, and is reportedly still owed more than $100 million in future guarantees. Specific terms of his deal are not public but its total value was widely believed to be well into the nine figures, with some initial reports suggesting it was worth more than $300 million. He made more than $106 million in on-course prize and bonus money during his three seasons at LIV, according to Spotrac .

Now, Rahm and LIV "are in advanced discussions for a consensual separation agreement," Beck said, which they hope to finalize on or before Oct. 15, with a goal of the court hearing it on Nov. 5.

Judge Michael Kaplan, who is overseeing the case, approved LIV's motion to reject all existing player contracts, excluding Rahm's. If a settlement is not reached by Nov. 5, Rahm intends to continue fighting LIV in court, according to Beck.

The news that Rahm plans to leave LIV is not surprising. He had been coy in recent months when asked about his future with the league, often noting he was still under contract but never committing to continuing to play.

Rahm was LIV's biggest star besides Bryson DeChambeau, although he has not won a major since leaving the PGA Tour after the 2023 season. Barring a special deal with the PGA Tour, he won't be eligible to return until at least next August—one year after his most recent LIV event. Rahm will remain eligible to compete on the DP World Tour and the Ryder Cup. He was scheduled to compete at this week's Spanish Open but withdrew due to the imminent birth of his fourth child.

LIV on Monday signed a long-awaited amended restructuring support agreement (RSA) with BC Partners—the private equity and credit firm set to provide $300 million of new financing for LIV post-bankruptcy—that includes an initial $4 million loan to aid with the Chapter 11 process. As part of that deal, BC Partners pushed back an Oct. 13 deadline for a "requisite number of players" to agree to new contracts with LIV to Oct. 25.

articles.title: Jon Rahm to quit LIV Golf over 'unacceptable' terms for proposed relaunch
articles.summary: Jon Rahm is set to quit LIV Golf after deeming the terms proposed to him for the relaunch of the series “unacceptable”; Rahm is reportedly owed up to $150m (£113m) from the contract he signed three years ago, with both sides now working towards a separation agreement
articles.body:
LIV Golf is currently going through Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the US after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its support at the end of the season, having invested $5bn (£3.7bn) over four years.

While players including Sergio Garcia successfully petitioned the court to lift the automatic stay on their contracts, effectively freeing them to explore other opportunities for next year, Rahm was not granted the same route out.

The Spaniard is one of LIV Golf's two biggest names, alongside Bryson DeChambeau, and is reportedly owed up to $150m (£113m) for the remainder of the contract he signed almost three years ago.

"Mr Rahm has independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0 and has determined that those terms are unacceptable to him, and he will not be participating going forward in LIV 2.0," attorney John Beck told a bankruptcy hearing.

The Athletic has also reported that Rahm and LIV are working towards a separation agreement, with a deal expected to be finalised by October 15.

Rahm withdrew from this week's Open de Espana in Madrid to remain at home with wife Kelley, who is expecting their fourth child.

The 31-year-old has already taken steps towards a potential return to the traditional tours. In May, he ended his dispute with the DP World Tour and paid around £2.21m in fines for playing in conflicting events, securing conditional releases for 2026 and making him eligible for the Ryder Cup.

Rahm previously declined the PGA Tour's offer of reinstatement through a specially created Returning Member Program, which was made available to him, Cameron Smith, Bryson DeChambeau and Brooks Koepka. Koepka was the only player to accept.

As a result, Rahm would face a mandatory one-year suspension before being eligible to return to the PGA Tour, meaning he could not play on the circuit until late August next year.

articles.title: Jon Rahm leaving LIV Golf, attorney reveals, dealing blow to bankrupt league
articles.summary: Jon Rahm will be departing LIV Golf, where he's spent the last three years.
articles.body:
Wherever LIV Golf goes from here, Jon Rahm won't be a part of it. The two-time major winner is exiting the league as it prepares to transition into its next phase, dubbed "LIV 2.0."

LIV Golf, formerly funded by Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, is attempting to reorganize itself into a worldwide tour with other investment. Rahm's departure is a crucial PR blow to the league, which had hoped to capitalize on the star power of its biggest names as it invited investment in its next phase.

Rahm's attorney John Beck announced at LIV's ongoing bankruptcy hearings that Rahm "has independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0 ... and has determined that those terms are unacceptable to him, and he will be not be participating going forward." LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on Sept. 8.

Still remaining to be determined: Where Rahm plays next, and whether LIV Golf has any remaining contractual hold on him. PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp has repeatedly stated that there is no pathway back to the Tour for any player with contractual ties to any outside Tour (i.e. LIV Golf). If Rahm is able to demonstrate that he is free of any legal entanglements, he could follow the path of fellow former LIV player Patrick Reed, who has spent a year working his way back onto the Tour via the DP World Tour and other international stops.

The contract status of Rahm and other LIV players is a key component of LIV's current reorganization. As recently as May, LIV CEO Scott O'Neil told Yahoo Sports that Rahm was still under contract to LIV for several years; one of the key questions for LIV's immediate future is whether those contracts are still enforceable or null and void as a result of LIV's bankruptcy proceedings.

Beck indicated in Wednesday's bankruptcy proceedings that Rahm and LIV are working on an exit agreement. LIV has granted Sergio Garcia a release from his deal, but Rahm's remains in question.

Rahm and fellow two-time major winner Bryson DeChambeau made for an attractive pitch to potential LIV investors, but DeChambeau is currently a free agent, and Rahm's departure makes LIV's pitch that much more difficult. Rahm, who is still owed somewhere in the neighborhood of $100 million, is apparently the largest creditor remaining for LIV Golf, as well as its key drawing card.

Rahm's departure for LIV in late 2023 was a significant coup for the breakaway tour, and seemed to herald that future potential defections would follow. But Rahm, as it turned out, was the last significant name to join LIV, which is now attempting to reorganize itself without Saudi funding.

As Golf.com's James Colgan noted , Rahm's three-year majors record while a member of LIV was a substantial downgrade from his prior run. While with LIV, Rahm played in 11 majors, winning zero, placing in the top 10 four times and the top 5 once while missing two cuts. In the three years prior to joining LIV, Rahm had 12 major starts, finished in the top 10 seven times, did not miss a cut, and won twice at the 2021 U.S. Open and 2023 Masters. Rahm has a lifetime exemption into the Masters; his exemptions to the Open Championship and PGA Championship run through the 2028 events, and his U.S. Open exemption runs through the 2031 event.

articles.title: Packers’ embarrassing statistic could lead to end of Matt LaFleur’s tenure
articles.summary: Packers' rushing struggles put LaFleur's future under scrutiny.
articles.body:
The NFL season has not started the way the Green Bay Packers hoped, and one alarming statistic through four weeks could put additional pressure on head coach Matt LaFleur.

The Packers have more penalty yards per game than rushing yards per game this season — Onyx Odds (@OnyxOdds) October 6, 2026

The Packers have more penalty yards per game than rushing yards per game this season

Despite entering Week 5 with a 2-2 record, Green Bay's running game has struggled to generate consistent production. Through the first four games of the 2026 season, the Packers are averaging more penalty yards per game than rushing yards, with 86.0 penalty yards compared to just 58.0 rushing yards per contest.

That imbalance has become one of the team's biggest concerns as Green Bay prepares for a crucial divisional matchup.

Green Bay Packers running back MarShawn Lloyd (32) runs with the ball as the New York Jets defend during a game at MetLife Stadium, Sep 20, 2026, East Rutherford, NJ, USA.

Some of the Packers' problems on the ground can be attributed to the absence of Josh Jacobs, their top running back. Jacobs is currently unavailable while dealing with off-field legal issues stemming from misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property.

Without Jacobs, Green Bay has relied on MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks to carry the rushing workload. However, none of the three has recorded a rushing touchdown through the first four games.

The Packers did show some improvement in Week 4, rushing for a season-high 86 yards during their 17-14 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. However, the overall numbers remain a concern for a team hoping to establish a more balanced offense.

The struggles on the ground have also placed more attention on LaFleur, who has been tasked with getting the offense back on track. While the Packers are still above .500, continued issues could increase pressure on the longtime head coach.

Following the Week 4 victory, LaFleur delivered a pointed message to his running backs when discussing ball security. "I think a great teacher is the bench," he said, emphasizing the importance of protecting the football.

Green Bay will have an immediate opportunity to address some of its offensive problems when the Packers host the division-rival Chicago Bears on Sunday.

Chicago enters Week 5 with a 3-1 record, making the matchup an important early-season test for Green Bay. A stronger rushing performance could help the Packers regain momentum, while another disappointing showing would only increase questions surrounding the team and its head coach.

The Saudi-backed breakaway league filed for bankruptcy last month, with its restructuring plan likely to release players from their existing contracts ahead of a potential LIV 2.0 relaunch.

The 2017 Masters champion would first need to regain his DP World Tour membership.

Garcia has also not ruled out a return to the PGA Tour, although under its rules he would have to serve a suspension until August.

articles.title: Is Packers Coach Matt LaFleur Cowardly — Or Clever — Not To Battle The Bears Ben Johnson?
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears meet Sunday at noon at Lambeau Field.
articles.body:
George Halas, who founded the Chicago Bears, and Green Bay Packers co-founder Earl "Curly" Lambeau" refused to shake hands after they met twice each season.

"Shake hands! That would have been a lie," Lambeau once said of Halas, his No. 1 rival. "If I lost, I wanted to punch Halas in the nose. If he lost, Halas wanted to punch me."

In the 1980s, Packers coach Forrest Gregg famously told his players, "You take care of the Bears and I'll take care of (Mike) Ditka."

In 2021, Green Bay quarterback Aaron Rodgers screamed at two Chicago Bears fans, "I've owned you all my f***ing life! I own you. I still own you."

Yes, the NFL's oldest rivalry is packed with countless stories of how much these two proud organizations dislike the other.

Now, for the past 21 months, Chicago head coach Ben Johnson has been poking Packers boss Matt LaFleur. Interestingly, LaFleur has taken one body blow after another, refusing to enter the ring with Johnson.

At Johnson's introductory press conference, the Bears' fiery new coach — who had been the offensive coordinator in Detroit — said: "To be quite frank with you, I kind of enjoyed beating Matt LaFleur twice a year."

• Won two of his three meetings with LaFleur, both in dramatic fashion. Chicago rallied from a 16-6 deficit with 2 minutes left in Week 16, 2025, and prevailed, 22-16, in overtime. The Bears then overcame a 21-3 halftime deficit and defeated Green Bay, 31-27, in the NFC Wild Card round.

• Screamed "F*** the Packers. F*** them," after Chicago's playoff win over Green Bay.

• Took part in three brief, icy handshakes with LaFleur in 2025.

• And said, "Who likes the Packers?" during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine.

LaFleur has been given multiple chances to punch back, but hasn't put on the gloves. Instead, he insists that worrying about what Johnson has to say is wasted energy, and accomplishes nothing come kickoff.

"This game is about players," said LaFleur, whose team hosts Chicago Sunday at noon (CST). "And so we'll keep it about the players."

While LaFleur has stayed quiet, some Packers certainly haven't been amused by Johnson's antics.

"I mean, he's dissing us," Green Bay left tackle Jordan Morgan said of Johnson. "He's dissing the Packers. A lot of people in here, I'm pretty sure, take that to heart. And we got a chance to prove to everybody on Sunday that we the best team."

When tight end Tucker Kraft was asked if Johnson screaming, "F*** the Packers" bothered him, he said: "Yes. Yeah. I guess. I talk with my pads, so I'll just wait 'til Sunday."

Linebacker Zaire Franklin, in his first year with Green Bay, already seems to understand the intensity of the rivalry.

"It's a lot of bad blood," Franklin said. "A lot of bad blood. A lot of genuine dislike."

Others viewed Johnson's chatter as nothing more than hot air, insisting football games aren't won during press conferences.

"My dad always told me, man, the loudest ones in the room, don't be scared of them," Green Bay defensive tackle Karl Brooks said. "They always be the quiet ones that get you. So if you're the loudest in the room talking, just … we just got to go out there and play. It's not about who's talking, who's poking at who. It's about what the players do in between the white lines."

"It's easy to have a camera in front of you and say whatever you want," Williams said. "You know that's not going to stop you from getting hit in the mouth on any given Sunday. And so to me, it's always been about the work, about how you show up on Sunday. The talk is, I mean, it's fluff to me."

Or as Packers center Sean Rhyan succinctly said of Johnson: "Let him talk. Doesn't mean (expletive)."

For the most part, LaFleur's record in this rivalry has done the talking.

LaFleur won his first 11 games against Chicago — eight with Rodgers at quarterback and three with Jordan Love. The tide has turned, though, with Chicago winning three of the last four contests — including the final two in 2025 when Green Bay had its two epic collapses.

As Green Bay's players sat in stunned silence — trying to wrap their heads around what happened during their playoff loss to the Bears in January — Johnson was yelling "F*** the Packers" a few doors down.

"Let's say we win that game last year, I'm sure there'd be some guys in the locker room saying the same thing (about the Bears)," Williams said.

Instead, it's Johnson and the Bears that are doing the talking right now. And LaFleur is taking the blows instead of punching back.

It's not the approach Lambeau, Gregg or Rodgers would have ever taken. But it's one LaFleur is sticking with.

"I'm not the one out there playing," LaFleur said. "So I think that's always been my mentality, and we're going to keep it about those guys."

Come late Sunday afternoon, we'll see if LaFleur's method was the right one.

articles.title: Packers tight end Tucker Kraft struggling with drops as he comes back from torn ACL
articles.summary: (AP) — Green Bay’s Tucker Kraft said this summer he believed he was playing as well as any tight end in the NFL before tearing his anterior cruciate ligament...
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay's Tucker Kraft said this summer he believed he was playing as well as any tight end in the NFL before tearing his anterior cruciate ligament last season.

Now that he's healthy again, Kraft has been unable to pick up right where he left off.

Kraft scored his first touchdown of the season Sunday in the Packers' 17-14 victory at Tampa Bay, but he also couldn't hang on to a pass in the end zone to continue his uncharacteristic struggles with drops. Kraft is averaging 9.9 yards per catch, well below his career average of 13.7 heading into the season.

"I think I'm just trying to do too much," Kraft said Wednesday. "Offensively, we might get into a lull, and I think I can make the game-saving play right there. I'm taking my eyes off the ball. Can't do anything without the ball, so I'm just going to slow down and play my role. Catch the football."

Kraft has caught 15 passes for 148 yards with one touchdown through four games heading into Sunday's matchup with the Chicago Bears (3-1).

Last season, he had 32 receptions for 489 yards and six touchdowns in eight games before tearing his right ACL in a Nov. 2 loss to the Carolina Panthers.

Packers coach Matt LaFleur says it's a matter of shaking off the rust.

"I think a lot of guys that come off major injuries, it takes a period of time," LaFleur said. "And I know we want instant gratification, and the expectation is whatever you saw that that's what it's going to be. But I think for many of these guys, not just us, but around the league, guys that come off major injuries, it just takes them some time. They've got to get back to playing."

Kraft worked his way back in time to be ready for the start of the season. He signed a four-year, $75 million contract extension with a maximum value of $92 million the day before the Packers (2-2) opened their season with a 39-22 loss at Minnesota.

But he's still working his way back to the form he showed in the first half of last season.

While Kraft acknowledges his numbers don't necessarily reflect it, the 2023 third-round pick from South Dakota State believes the game is slowing down for him. He says he's "feeling more savvy" in his coverage recognition.

"Statistically, it might not look like I'm playing better," Kraft said. "Some would even say that I might've lost my stinger. My brothers were telling me that. They said, 'You look like you kind of lost your edge out there.' They said it to me last week. I tried to go out in Tampa and be a meanie, but it was too damn hot. I couldn't breathe out there.

"This week, (I'll) try to get back to my roots, the kind of (stuff) I was on my first and second year when I was playing to the echo of the whistle and being hard on the defense."

He set up Green Bay's first touchdown Sunday by taking a direct snap on fourth-and-1 from the 9 and delivering a 3-yard run, with quarterback Jordan Love coming up from behind to push him forward.

"I was a quarterback in high school for two years, did a little under center," Kraft said. "I got a lot of experience in college running that play because it's a special situation and you have to practice it a lot in college, and we ran it like eight times when I was at South Dakota State."

That's one way Kraft has added to his game while he attempts to improve his production.

After all, he doesn't merely want to get back to playing the way he did last season. He wants to be even better.

"The goal is always to ascend," Kraft said. "If you're not getting better, you're getting worse. So, my goal is to walk in this building every day with the right mindset. See the film, see our run/pass pictures, and really just apply it with all the reps that I've had throughout my time here since 2023. So, yeah, now like I said, I'm just trying to continue to evolve, get some more of those breakout on-the-field plays. That all starts with catching the ball."

articles.title: PGA Tour: England's Jordan Smith starts well at Baycurrent Classic as Jacob Bridgeman leads in Japan

Smith, who has made 17 of 23 cuts and recorded eight top-25 finishes with a best of third at the Valspar Championship since earning a PGA Tour card for 2026, registered four birdies on his front nine and three coming home at Yokohama Country Club.

The Baycurrent Classic, formerly known as the Zozo Championship, was first played in 2019 when Tiger Woods took the title after beating home player Hideki Matsuyama by three strokes.

articles.title: Aramco Korea Championship: Suzann Pettersen shoots even par in first round on Ladies European Tour after four years
articles.summary: Suzann Pettersen makes return to Ladies European Tour for first time since 2022 and rallies after early dropped shots to card even-par 72, including monster birdie at 15; England's Lily May Humphreys in share of second after five-under 67; watch second round from 5.30am Friday
articles.body:
Pettersen, 45, retired after sinking the winning putt for Team Europe in the 2019 Solheim Cup at Gleneagles, with her only appearance since the 2022 Aramco Team Series event in Jeddah.

The Norwegian - who captained Europe at the 2023 and 2024 Solheim Cups - was three over after six holes in South Korea, bogeying the third and double bogeying the sixth.

But the two-time major winner rallied with birdies at eight, 13 and 15 - picking up a shot at the last of those holes with a monster putt - and went bogey-free on her back nine.

Humphreys: I had quite a lot of good fortune go my way

Humphreys - who won her sole Ladies European Tour title to date at the 2023 Joburg Ladies Open - carded a five-under 67 to sit one shot behind leader Patricie Mackova.

Like Pettersen, the 24-year-old dropped shots at three and six, but she registered five birdies as well as an eagle at the par-five 13th to match the rounds of Miyu Yamashita, Sarah Kemp and Olivia Cowan.

Humphreys said: "I played very nicely and I had quite a lot of good fortune go my way which you need around here to shoot a low number. The course doesn't give you anything. You need to earn every birdie and some pars.

"I holed an insane amount of long putts and the hole-out for eagle which was a nice way to start the afternoon"

There have been four English winners on the Ladies European Tour in 2026.

Charley Hull won the season-opening PIF Saudi Ladies International in February, with Esme Hamilton then claiming a maiden title on the tour with victory at the South African Women's Open in April.

Eleanor Givens secured her first LET victory at the VP Bank Swiss Ladies Open in August, while Charlotte Heath did likewise at the La Sella Open in September.

Mackova wore green to raise awareness around sustainability, saying afterwards: "Myself, Sara [Kouskova], Celina [Sattelkau], and Camille [Chevalier] are part of an organisation called EcoAthletes.

articles.title: Hate crime figures rise after more offences motivated by religion and race, figures show
articles.summary: Figures supplied by police forces suggest nearly 150,000 hate crimes were recorded between April 2025 and March 2026
articles.body:
Hate crimes in England and Wales increased by 7% in the year up to March 2026, rising to nearly 147,000, data released by the Home Office suggested.

Figures supplied to the government by police forces indicated a rise from more than 137,000 offences recorded in the previous year.

The Home Office said the figures "may suggest there has been a genuine increase" in hate crimes, driven by rises in offences linked to race and religion.

The data also suggested recorded hate crimes linked to sexual orientation, disability and transgender identity were unchanged or falling.

Policing Minister Sarah Jones said the rising figures were "a stark warning that hatred continues to blight our communities".

Hate crime in England and Wales rises for first time in three years

"We are delivering the biggest reforms to policing in over 200 years, alongside record funding to protect Muslim and Jewish people and places of worship," she added.

The Home Office said there were a total of 146,825 hate crimes recorded by police in the two nations in the year to March 2026.

Racially-motivated offences accounted for the majority of all police recorded hate crimes, at around 74%, with about 8% of other hate crimes classified as religious.

The Home Office said the rise in these offences over the last year was due to an increase in public order offences, often taking the form of intimidation and abuse, but crimes involving violence and vandalism were also included in the statistics.

"In the last two years, there has been a rise in hate crime offences that is not seen in the overall violent and public order offences trend," the report said.

"This may suggest there has been a genuine increase in hate crime offences over the last two years."

Where the ethnicity of the victim was known in the race and religion related hate crimes, around one third of victims were identified as Asian and around a quarter as black.

The Home Office said that it was likely that hate crime "offences against white victims will include xenophobic abuse against people not born in the UK".

The figures showed a 13% rise in religious hate crimes recorded by police during the year to March 2026, with 11,419 recorded offences in total.

Of those there was a 15% rise in hate crimes targeting Muslims and 10% increase in those that targeted Jewish people.

The increase in hate crimes targeting Muslims (from 4,479 to 5,132 offences) showed a particular rise in September of last year, which the Home Office said "coincided with a number of protests and incidents of public order".

There were hate crimes targeting both Muslims and Jewish people following the start of the war in Iran launched by the US and Israel in the spring of this year.

Antisemitic hate crimes have been at elevated levels since the beginning of the conflict between Israel and Hamas in 2023, but saw a spike in October 2025 following the fatal attack at the Heaton Park Synagogue in Manchester.

Other attacks followed in the months after, including in March when four Jewish community ambulances were torched in Golders Green, north London. Prosecutors say the incident was a targeted attack against the Jewish community.

articles.summary: El neozelandés Daniel Hillier embocó de un golpe en el hoyo 17 y se lleva un BMW iX5
articles.body: Daniel Hillier ha pegado el golpe perfecto en el hoyo 17 (par 3) del Club de Campo Villa de Madrid para llevarse un premio excepcional. El neozelandés de 28 años, que actualmente ocupa el puesto 101 del ranking mundial, ganó un BMW iX5 gracias a su impecable golpe. Aunque la bandera del el hoyo 17 del Club de Campo siempre está bien protegida por tres bunkers, en el riesgo está la ganancia. Con un hierro en la mano, la bola de Hillier recorrió los 170 metros que la separaban del hoyo para aterrizar de forma muy limpia. Como el campo está más blando debido a las lluvias de estos días, la bola casi se clavó. Es cierto que se trata de un hoyo en uno de par 3, pero el citado premio lleva en juego varios años y nadie lo había conseguido. Hillier, que sólo cuenta en su palmarés con un torneo del DP World Tour, podrá presumir de hazaña y de coche.

articles.title: US bars Microsoft, Adobe, and major IT firms from green card program for skilled foreign workers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The other firms being suspended from the program include Capgemini, Cognizant, HCL, Infosys, Tata, and Wipro.
articles.body:
The Trump administration is suspending Microsoft, Adobe, and several other technology companies from a program that helps skilled foreign workers obtain permanent residency in the United States, accusing the companies of fraud.

“Our ​message to Microsoft is: You’re a great American company, ​but you’ve got to hire great American workers,” U.S. ⁠Vice President JD Vance said in a news conference on Thursday, Reuters reported.

The other firms being suspended from the program include Capgemini, Cognizant, HCL, Infosys, Tata, and Wipro. Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling said the government would not accept any new or pending permanent ​labor certification applications involving these companies.

H-1B visas are designed for highly skilled positions that employers may struggle to fill with qualified U.S. workers. Tech companies are among the largest users of the program, with nearly three-quarters of approved visas going to workers from India, according to The Associated Press .

“We believe in the strength and talent of the American workforce,” a Microsoft spokesperson said in an email to TechCrunch. “That is why the vast majority of Microsoft employees in the United States are Americans. We look forward to providing the Administration with additional information. For example, of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications we submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% percent were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees.”

The statement continues, “These were not to hire new people. The remaining filings for new employees were for individuals already legally in the United States who decided to come work for us, and they equal only 1% of our U.S. workforce. They are not new arrivals to our country.”

The company went on to note that it only files H-1B petitions for those who meet the “rigorous standards” of the visa category, and that pays its H-1B employees the same as any “other employees doing comparable work.”

Vance also said during the news conference that the administration would investigate nine universities, including Harvard, Yale, and Stanford, over allegations they’re abusing a program that allows international students to come to the U.S. and were using the program to undermine wages for American workers.

Adobe did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: DP World Tour: Scotland's Connor Syme and Grant Forrest amongst leaders after first round of Open de España with Sergio Garcia one back
articles.summary: There is a three-way tie for the lead after the first round of the Open de Espana; Sergio Garcia sits one shot back; The Open de Espana continues on Friday October 9 from 1pm on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Starting on the 10th, Syme made a quick start with back-to-back birdies then rolled in a 52-foot putt at the 15th as he headed into the turn five under.

A tap-in birdie at the fourth saw Syme take the solo lead at Real Club de Campo Villa de Madrid, but he was then not able to save par on the eighth after finding the rough off the tee.

Forrest also started his round on the back nine and after two bogeys, on 13 and then three, he finished strongly with a run of three birdies through the closing six holes.

Eugenio Chacarra made the lowest first round in seven appearances at his national open with a 66, which included two eagles as well as three bogeys, to also share the lead.

However, he is struggling with pain and will assess how he feels over the next 24 hours.

"It's not good, suffering a lot. It's been tough, not sure what is going to happen tomorrow," Chacarra said after his round.

"I need to take care of myself. Obviously, I got a good round but how I feel physically is not great.

"It doesn't hurt when I'm swinging, so I can still make a score but it's been really tough to walk.

"The pain I had on the last 12 holes, I don't know if it is worth it as I have a lot to play the next couple of weeks.

"I've got 24 hours to rest and see how it feels in the morning. I've got a lot to play for, I've got four weeks that are really important to me."

Garcia, whose stay with LIV Golf appears to be coming to an end, is in a group at four under, with an eagle on the fourth and four birdies offsetting two bogeys.

Daniel Hillier landed the keys to a new BMW iX5 with his first hole-in-one on the DP World Tour at the par-three 17th.

"I wasn't too happy with the strike," Hillier said.

"I was telling it to go the whole way, but it kind of hung in the air for a little bit longer than I thought, and then, yeah, heard some cheers - a little bit of disbelief for a while, but it's nice to see it go in."

The New Zealander went on to finish in the group alongside Garcia, Spain's Angel Ayora and Dane Jacob Skov Olesen, whose 67 was blemish-free.

Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed, though, had a frustrating round on his return from injury, finishing down the field at two over.

The Open de Espana continues on Friday October 9 from 1pm on Sky Sports Golf.

articles.title: Government approves major Green Hill Solar Farm in Northants
articles.summary: Officials say the development will help with energy security, but local MPs opposed the farm.
articles.body:
The government has approved what could be one of the UK's largest solar farms.

Green Hill Solar Farm would cover about 2,965 acres (1,200 hectares) of land south and west of Wellingborough and north of Northampton.

It would also extend to include land to the northeast of Warrington, a hamlet in Buckinghamshire.

Baroness Curran, from the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, said on approving the development: "Solar power is crucial to delivering energy security for the country and financial security for communities, families and businesses."

The size of the project meant that recommendations for the scheme were made by the Planning Inspectorate, rather than local planning authorities.

The inspectorate's examination stage took more than five months to complete, opening in October 2025 and closing in April.

More than 1,200 people and businesses sent comments about the plans.

Campaigners opposing the proposal argued that solar panels up to 4.5m (15ft) high could "devastate the Northamptonshire countryside".

Sarah Bool and Stuart Andrew, the Conservative MPs for South Northamptonshire and Daventry respectively, both opposed the development and handed a petition into Downing Street.

Green Hill Solar said the farm would "benefit Britain with clean, secure, low-cost energy".

It said the scheme could generate 500 megawatts of electricity to power about 200,000 homes.

It is hoped construction will begin in 2027, with the aim of providing electricity to homes by 2029, the company said.

articles.title: Sergio García saca a relucir su mejor versión en el Open de España
articles.standfirst: Firma 67 golpes (-4) y está a uno de los líderes, entre los que se encuentra Eugenio Chacarra
articles.summary: Firma 67 golpes (-4) y está a uno de los líderes, entre los que se encuentra Eugenio Chacarra
articles.body: Hace ya 24 años de la victoria de Sergio García en el Open de España de Gran Canaria y todavía es muy pronto para saber si tendrá la oportunidad de pelear por el título el domingo, pero tras la primera ronda el castellonense puede decir que va por el buen camino. El de Borriol firmó 67 golpes (-4) y está a uno de los colíderes, entre los que se encuentra el protagonista del día, Eugenio Chacarra (66). El madrileño, con el tercer dedo del pie derecho roto, cuajó una magnífica actuación. La solidez de Ángel Ayora (68) de tee a green durante el turno matinal también lo aúpan a lo más alto. Por parte de la ‘Armada’, también Manuel Elvira (69) jugó bajo par y al par del campo están David Puig, Quim Vidal, Alfredo García-Heredia, Josele Ballester y Alejandro del Rey. Entre las grandes estrellas internacionales no hubo vueltas de relumbrón, pero Francesco Molinari y Shane Lowry lograron materializar 70 golpes. Ludvig Aberg, otro de los nombres importantes del torneo, sufrió desde el tee y se tuvo que conformar con el par. La vuelta Sergio García, que jugó con Justin Rose y el campeón defensor Marco Penge, dejó muy buenas sensaciones de cara lo que viene y eso que en el turno de tarde los greenes estuvieron mucho más complicados. Salió por el hoyo 1 y en el 4 logró un eagle que supuso un gran impulso, porque el español venía jugando perfecto a tee a green pero no le sacaba partido. En el green del 6 se atascó, pero no así su juego. La mejor versión de García ha emergido esta semana en el Club de Campo. En el 12, pese a una mala salida, se llevó el birdie; en el 13 también erró desde el tee y fue a un bunker y todo acabó en bogey. Sin embargo, a partir de ahí todo se volvió a ajustar. El ganador del Masters 2017 se mostró muy satisfecho con su vuelta: "Estoy contento de haber jugado bien en una tarde tan complicada con viento racheado, greenes un poquito pesados y el campo blando. He jugado sólido. [...] He fallado sólo un green, desde el tee he estado muy bien, he fallado sólo tres o cuatro calles, que está muy bien para lo complicado que se está jugando. Creo que todo mi juego ha estado muy bien, incluido el juego corto y el putt". Sobre las recientes noticias de que Rahm y Puig dejarán LIV, García valoró: "Cada uno hace lo que cree que es mejor para él y para su familia. Yo respaldo lo que hagan. A mí ayer en el juzgado me dieron cancha con la apelación que pusimos".

articles.title: Arrow Co-Creator Shares Details and Concept Art for Canceled Green Lantern Show That Shares Striking Similarities to HBO's Lanterns
articles.summary: Concept art for a canceled Green Lanterns show has been shared online by a co-creator of the CW’s Arrow series, showing what the Emerald Knights’ adventures almost looked like before HBO pivoted to Lanterns, instead.
articles.body:
Concept art for a canceled Green Lanterns show has been shared online by a co-creator of the CW’s Arrow series, showing what the Emerald Knights’ adventures almost looked like before HBO pivoted to Lanterns, instead.

Marc Guggenheim, who helped spearhead the CW’s Arrowverse franchise, showed off the artwork on his Substack on October 7, which consisted of three separate pieces. He also shared some trivia about the series’ plot, which shared some similarities to HBO’s Lanterns .

The first of these similarities is that this canceled show, titled Emerald Knights, would have taken place in two different time periods. Manhunters were the primary villains of the series, who also served as the central antagonists of Lanterns (in a way, at least).

“I have to reach into my memory to recall other bits of trivia like that, but I do remember that our original take took place in two time periods and had the Manhunters as the primary villains and my original title pitch was Emerald Knights,” Guggenheim said.

The first piece of artwork that he shared showed a group of Green Lanterns fending off a horde of attacking aliens using various projections like a bo staff, a sword, and shields. According to Guggenheim, this artwork was supposed to portray the opening of the show’s pilot episode.

“I wish I could remember the name of the artist that did this piece. It was concept art for the opening sequence of our Pilot," he wrote.

Emerald Knights Concept Art Shared by Marc Guggenheim

The last two images were character-focused, showing early looks at Guy Gardener and another Lantern that many fans might assume is Jo Mullein at first glance. This artwork notably included the faces of actors Finn Wittrock and Jenelle Monae, respectively; Monae’s inclusion isn’t a huge surprise, though, given that writer N.K. Jemisin and comic artist Jamal Campbell used her likeness to design Mullein’s visual look. However, Guggenheim clarified that this artwork wasn’t portraying Mullein, but instead was an original character created specifically for the show.

"No, this isn’t Jo Mullein. This is the costume design by Laura Jean Shannon for a new character we had created for the series,” he said. He also gave some more information about Gardner’s costume, saying it was planned to be altered “slightly” in order to reflect his Justice League International design.

HBO’s Lanterns was a smash hit , and has already entered early development for a second season , according to the show’s co-creator. While it’s certainly interesting to think about what Guggenheim’s canceled Emerald Knights series could have done with the source material, it’s safe to say that Lanterns’ showrunners knocked it out of the park, earning rave reviews from hardcore fans and critics alike.

For more Lanterns news, check out our interview with Aaron Pierre, Kyle Chandler, and executive producers Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King, where they delve into their mission for the show’s first season and why they decided to take a different approach to its final conflict.

articles.title: US suspends Microsoft from Green Card sponsorship programme; company responds: Microsoft only files H-1B petitions for those who...
articles.summary: The US government has suspended Microsoft from the Permanent Labor Certification Program (PERM), the process most employers must clear before sponsoring a
articles.body: The US government has suspended Microsoft from the Permanent Labor Certification Program (PERM), the process most employers must clear before sponsoring a foreign worker for a Green Card. Vice President JD Vance and Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling announced the move at a press conference in Washington on October 8, and the Labor Department will now neither accept new PERM applications from Microsoft nor process the ones already pending.Vance singled out the company as the worst offender. "There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft," he said, claiming Microsoft laid off around 6,000 American workers last year while employing 6,300 people on H-1B visas and securing nearly 3,000 Green Cards. Microsoft has pushed back, saying the vast majority of its US employees are Americans.A Vance-led fraud probe is behind Microsoft's PERM suspensionThe suspension follows an investigation by an anti-fraud task force that Vance chairs. Officials argued that PERM is meant for roles needing "hyper-specialized" skills that are hard to find in the US, and accused Microsoft of misrepresenting its needs to replace American staff with cheaper foreign hires."The H-1B visa is how the people get into the United States in the first place, and then a PERM program is how those employees stay," Vance said. He also claimed that for every worker Microsoft laid off, it brought in "one and a half foreign indentured servants." Sonderling said Microsoft was suspended "due to multiple active federal investigations."Microsoft is the largest filer of PERM applications, according to Labor Department data, so the freeze puts a sizeable pipeline of employee Green Card cases on hold.Microsoft says most of its H-1B filings were for existing employeesMicrosoft responded with a blog post on Thursday. It said about 80% of the roughly 6,000 H-1B applications it filed in the last fiscal year were to extend or change the status of existing employees, not to hire new people. The rest were for people already living legally in the US, and they make up only 1% of its US workforce."Microsoft only files H-1B petitions for those who meet the rigorous standards of this visa category," the company said. It added that its H-1B wages are among the highest of all filings, and that these employees are paid the same as anyone else doing comparable work.Data from Levels.fyi places Microsoft fourth among H-1B sponsors this year, with 21,706 petitions at a median base salary of $180,710. The company also said in July it would cut 4,800 jobs, or about 2.1% of its global workforce.Vance says the Microsoft suspension will last "as long as it needs to"Vance did not spell out what Microsoft must do to regain access to the programme. "Our message to Microsoft is not that we want to harm your company, it's that we want your company to thrive, but we want it to thrive by employing and empowering your fellow Americans," he said.The timing stood out. Hours later, President Donald Trump was due to present Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, the country's highest honour for tech achievement. Just over a week earlier, India-born Nadella, who joined Microsoft in 1992, sat two seats from Vance at a White House luncheon on AI.The move extends a wider crackdown on skilled-worker visas ahead of the November midterms, which last September brought a one-time $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions. For Microsoft employees already in the queue, the wait was long to begin with: PERM applications took an average of 336 days to process in August. Now it has no end date at all.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'We've got to get into the grind': Pat Cummins urges Australia to move beyond individual brilliance
articles.summary: Pat Cummins is emphasizing the importance of adopting a patient approach as Australia prepares for their Test match against South Africa. Given the fast-pace...
articles.body:
Australia have often thrived on explosive individual performances, but Pat Cummins wants his team to prepare for a very different kind of Test challenge against South Africa: one where patience, discipline and the ability to grind out sessions could matter more than spectacular moments. With the first Test beginning at Kingsmead on Friday, Cummins acknowledged that Australia cannot always rely on a Travis Head hundred or a Mitchell Starc burst to swing matches in their favour. With conditions expected to fluctuate on a traditionally tricky Durban surface, the captain believes his side must be ready to adapt to whatever the game throws at them.

Australia's recent Test cricket has often been fast-paced. Their last Test against Bangladesh in August finished inside two days, while two of the five Ashes Tests against England last summer also ended within two days. Cummins feels that has meant his side has not had enough opportunities to practise grinding their way through long, attritional contests. "For the batsmen and for the bowling group as well, getting into that grind is important. We haven't played too many of those kinds of Test matches in the last few years, particularly in Australia," Cummins said at his pre-match press conference. "They've been quite fast-paced. A lot of our success has come off big moments, be it a Travis Head century or Starcy (fast bowler Mitchell Starc) running through the top order," he added.

Cummins knows those match-winning bursts remain part of Australia's identity, but he wants his players to be comfortable when there are no quick breakthroughs or whirlwind innings. "I think we've got to get a little bit better, and we can get a bit better getting into the grind, It might not be the glamorous stuff, but it's that grinding out of sessions, not these whirlwind innings at times. Whatever tempo gets thrown at us or what the game needs, we must make sure we match that," he said.

Australia have also delayed naming their playing XI, with Cummins revealing that the selectors wanted another look at the Kingsmead surface before making the final call. "We don't know our team at this stage; the selectors will come down here and we'll just want to have one more look at the ground," he said. The visitors have some selection decisions to make, particularly in the batting department. Cameron Green is unavailable, while Josh Inglis is also absent, leaving Australia to weigh up different combinations. "We're trying to work out what we think is the best batting line-up for these conditions. Obviously, Cam Green's out and Josh Inglis isn't here as well," Cummins said.

Rather than simply replacing the missing players like-for-like, Cummins suggested Australia are considering how different combinations could best suit the conditions. "So that's a couple of changes that we've got to match up. What are the conditions going to throw at us? We've got a full squad. Everyone brings something a little bit different and it's just trying to work out what we think the best combinations are," he added.
